_comment: Every concurrency escape in the app target, with the invariant that makes it safe. Enforced by tools/test_concurrency_audit.py: a new escape with no entry fails the build gate, as does an entry whose file no longer has an escape. `make strict-concurrency` is the compiler half; this is the reasoning half.

escapes.invariant: Mutable state (owners, cleanupOwner, temporaryWorkers, producing, produced) is read and written only while `lock` is held; nearly every method is `lock.lock(); defer { lock.unlock() }`. No method calls out to other code while holding the lock, so a re-entrant call from `setTaskCompleted`-style callbacks cannot deadlock.
Immutable stored closure. It runs in `deinit`, which may happen on any thread; the closure only calls back into the lock-protected registry, which is safe from any thread. No other state.

@Published properties are written on the main thread only. The verification path in DownloadManager+PackageImport.swift runs on a utility queue but wraps every model mutation in DispatchQueue.main.async, and both URLSessions deliver delegate callbacks on delegateQueue .main. The reference is passed across boundaries; the fields are not written there. A worker reading the fields directly (rather than a copied snapshot) would be unsound - BackgroundDownloadMonitor reads them on @MainActor and copies values for exactly this reason.
escapes.watch: This is the escape most likely to stop being true. Any new off-main writer must be paired with a main-actor hop, not a direct assignment.

escapes.invariant: The owning UnifiedTaskCenter is @MainActor and there are no detached or global-queue tasks in the file; every mutation goes through the center on the main actor. The Sendable conformance exists so a reference can be handed to async signing/install work, not so those can mutate it.

`writable` and all IO run on the single serial `queue` (label VexSign.task-history), established in init and accessed only inside `queue.async` blocks. Serial queue ordering is the synchronisation. Note: `writable = true` is set in several branches of `load` but not on the .blocked(.inaccessible) path, which is deliberate - an unreadable journal must never become writable.

One import's private scratch object; `_ipa`, `uniqueWorkDirPayload` and `_didAddToDatabase` are mutated only from its own sequential async methods (copy -> extract -> move -> addDatabase -> clean). The only cross-thread touch is `download.unpackageProgress`, wrapped in DispatchQueue.main.async at the extract progress callback.
escapes.watch: Safe only while the pipeline stays sequential per instance. Two steps run concurrently on one handler would race on `_ipa` and `uniqueWorkDirPayload`.
